title: NorthBay Biosystems onprem intake - raw notes
content:
Context:
- Customer: NorthBay Biosystems (regulated diagnostics vendor). Interested in private on-prem Redwood control plane with inference runtime inside their air-gapped lab network.
- Call 2025-02-11, 10:00 PST. Attendees: Maya (RSE), Jordan (solutions), Riley (product PM), Dr. Anika Rao (NorthBay CTO), Samir Patel (infra lead), Elena (security/compliance).

High-level asks / constraints (verbatim-ish):
- Full data isolation: no egress from lab VLAN except to our optional control-plane proxy (they will vet).
- KMS integration: customer-managed keys (HSM-backed) for model artifacts and logs.
- Model pinning + reproducible rollout: must be able to pin model versions and rollback within 5m.
- Low-latency inference for 512-token seqs: p50 < 40ms, p95 < 120ms for their hotspot workflows.
- Throughput: baseline 50 concurrent requests, spiky to 200 for short bursts.
- Auditing: token-level usage logs retained 1 year; must support export to Splunk/SIEM via S3-compatible bucket in their network.
- Software lifecycle: customer wants ability to apply security patches on their cadence; we need a documented upgrade path and compatibility matrix.

Key technical notes from Samir (infra):
- Cluster: k8s 1.27 on bare-metal, 8 node pool for inference (A100-like hardware), separate control-plane nodes in DMZ.
- Network: strict egress policy, only whitelisted FQDNs allowed; prefer a pull-only control channel so agents initiate connections.
- Storage: NFS-backed model store, ceph block for runtime KV; encryption at rest mandatory.
- Identity: LDAP + mTLS for intra-cluster services.

Gotchas / open questions (need answers):
1) HSM integration shape: do they require PKCS#11 or an HSM-as-a-service appliance? Samir: "hardware HSM, PKCS#11". Need sample config for Redwood to use PKCS#11.
2) Control plane connectivity: they prefer a reverse-tunnel agent. Does our private package support agent-initiated control channel without opening inbound ports? (Action: confirm with eng-private-deployments runtime team).
3) Telemetry export: Splunk in-network uses HTTP collector with cert pinning. Need a delivery pattern for token-level logs without exfil. Option: push logs to local S3 gateway — confirm size/bandwidth.
4) Model size & quantization: they want to serve both 13B float and quantized 7B for burst fallback. Confirm recommended quantization format and expected throughput numbers for their A100 equivalent.
5) SLA timing: they asked about RPO for rollbacks (they want <5 minutes). Need to clarify what parts of the stack that includes (image rollout + model rollout + cache invalidation).

Immediate action items (owner initials):
- Maya: produce a security-hardened install checklist for agent-initiated control channel (due 2025-02-17).
- Jordan: prototype PKCS#11 integration example and share a minimal config + test script (due 2025-02-19).
- Riley: draft pilot SOW (4-week pilot: 2 weeks deploy & config, 2 weeks load/latency validation) and cost outline (due 2025-02-21).
- Samir/Elena (NorthBay): provide list of allowed egress FQDNs and Splunk endpoint cert fingerprint.

Pilot validation plan (sketch):
1) Deploy private control plane in staging (air-gapped test VLAN) with agent-initiated tunnel. Verify no inbound ports opened.
2) Provision HSM-backed KMS with PKCS#11; verify key wrap/unwrap flow for model artifacts.
3) Deploy 13B and quantized 7B variants; run synthetic load to measure p50/p95 for 512-token sequences.
4) Burst test: 200 concurrent short requests for 60s, measure latency tail and GPU utilization.
5) Audit export: push token-level logs to local S3 gateway and validate Splunk ingestion.
6) Failover test: simulate node loss and validate automatic fallback to quantized variant and model rollback within target time.

Preliminary config snippets (informal):
- Agent tunnel idea:
  - agent --control-url https://control-proxy.northbay.local --reverse-tunnel --auth-token <token> --cert /etc/agent/cert.pem
- PKCS#11 example (placeholder):
  - kms_config: |
      provider: pkcs11
      module_path: /usr/lib/opensc-pkcs11.so
      slot: 0
      token_label: "NORTHBAY-HSM"
- Deployment hint: nodeAffinity for GPU nodes + taint + dedicated namespace redwood-inference-private

Risk register (brief):
- R1: HSM driver incompatibilities with our runtime (mitigation: early test with customer's HSM dev kit).
- R2: Network policy prevents telemetry - may require on-prem SIEM adapter (mitigation: build small log forwarder container).
- R3: Latency targets not met for 13B float under burst (mitigation: burst autoscaler + fallback to quantized 7B + prewarmed model instances).
- R4: Patch window mismatch (mitigation: document non-breaking upgrade path and offer support for patching during pilot).

Notes to self (Maya) - non-prod reminders:
- Bring a lab HSM dev kit to next onsite.
- Run our private demo with reverse-tunnel agent before next call (target 2025-02-18).
- Validate our telemetry shim can write to object store behind NAT.

Communication snippets for customer (can copy into email):
- "Thanks for the call — attached is a short pilot SOW and a checklist of infra items we need to get started (HSM access, allowed egress list, Splunk cert). We will prototype PKCS#11 integration and the agent-initiated control channel this week and share results by EOD 2025-02-19."

Longer-term asks to product (for backlog):
- First-class pkcs11 KMS backend in private package with documented examples and test harnesses.
- Built-in local SIEM exporter with configurable scrubbing and S3 gateway support.
- UI surface for model pinning + rollback policy that shows estimated rollback time and cache-invalidations.

Misc / scraps (toss these if not used):
- Elena said: "must keep raw tokens for 1 year, but only hashes in user-facing UIs" — need to confirm retention policy and data minimization details.
- Suggestion: include a small raft-based KV for model-state to speed rollbacks (Riley to evaluate complexity).

Next meeting: 2025-02-25, 10:00 PST (tentative) - goal: review SOW and PKCS#11 prototype.

--- end of raw notes ---
